To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
maternal salt and fructose diet during pregnancy can have long term effects on the offspring's metabolic and cardiovascular status.
a high salt and high fructose maternal diet can affect the offspring's cardiovascular function in a sex specific and time dependent manner and produce a phenotype resembling NAFLD.
a maternal dietary intake of moderate salt and fructose, prior to and during pregnancy, can affect the adult offspring cardiovascular health.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a high salt and fructose diet on the mother, fetus and offspring.
the effect of maternal dietary salt and fructose consumption on offspring health.
the effects of the Western diet on maternal and fetal development.

the effects on maternal diet on offspring health are subtle and may be dependent on the sex of the offspring.

the maternal diet is an important factor in the development of the offspring and that the maternal diet has the capacity to affect the offspring in a number of different ways, both short and long term, which can affect the cardiovascular and metabolic status of the adult offspring and may be a contributing factor to the development of hypertension in later life.
the maternal dietary consumption of salt and frucose prior to, during and after pregnancy can have profound and long lasting effects on offspring cardiovascular and metabolic health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
maternal fructose intake can have a significant effect on maternal and fetal metabolic and cardiovascular health, which can be further enhanced by the addition of dietary salt.
maternal dietary fructose intake can increase the risk of offspring developing metabolic syndrome and maternal salt intake can increase offspring risk of developing hypertension.
maternal salt and fructose consumption can have a detrimental effect on the health and well being of the offspring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modern Western diet, high in salt and simple sugars can have detrimental effects on maternal, fetal, and offspring cardiovascular health and metabolic status.
maternal diet has a long lasting influence on offspring physiology, metabolism, growth and cardiovascular health.
maternal diet can have profound effects on fetal and adult offspring cardiovascular health.
